title: A result-focused construction suppresses the agent but preserves the affected item
summary: A result-focused construction licenses omission of an agent slot while retaining an explicitly affected item; an ordinary action construction requires both roles or marks an omitted agent separately.

design.unit: paired action/result records with candidate agent and affected-item positions
design.contrast: agent-suppressed result versus ordinary agentive action
design.prediction: When the result construction is selected, affected-item marking remains stable while agent marking may be absent; ordinary action frames should not show the same omission under matched inputs.
design.countermodel: A context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial packaging could produce the same surface distribution without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: Agent omission co-occurs equally with non-result actions, or result records omit the affected item rather than only the agent.
design.principal_risk: Agent and patient meanings are not independently bound. Related to action/result families but targets role suppression and preservation, not result latency.
